A PERSONAL INTRODUCTION

The opportunity
I see at Elliman.

Attract exceptional producers. Help them thrive. Earn their loyalty.

That’s what draws me to this role. I see an opportunity to help architect a cohesive national growth platform: a clear value proposition for established agents and teams, consistent recruiting discipline, and an agent experience that earns long-term commitment. Net growth means retention and recruitment belong in the same conversation.

At Side, I helped build a strategic partnerships function and expand a brokerage into six new markets. Since then, I’ve built a revenue organization from founder-led selling. I would bring both experiences to Elliman: understanding the brokerage partnership decision and creating shared standards that strengthen a national organization while respecting local market expertise.

WHY THIS ROLE

One national platform.
Local market strength.

01

Attract established producers.

I’ve built new markets through strategic partnerships. My focus would be on established agents and teams who strengthen Elliman’s luxury position—understanding their ambitions, evaluating the economics, and making a credible case for the move.

02

Create cohesion across regions.

I’ve developed leaders, managed sales teams, and built operating cadences. I would partner with regional leadership on shared targeting, coaching, reporting, and recruiting standards, while leaving room for relationships and local market judgment.

03

Make retention part of growth.

At Side, I worked across functions to support partner activation. I would apply that same discipline to producer integration, early productivity, and ongoing engagement. The promises made in recruiting must show up in the experience agents receive.

HOW I WOULD BEGIN

Listen carefully.
Build deliberately.

A proposed first-90-days approach, refined with Elliman’s leadership and regional teams.

START WITH THE PEOPLE AND THE FACTS

Understand what earns
an agent’s commitment.

Spend time with regional leaders, recruiters, recently recruited producers, and established teams. Understand why agents join, what makes them stay, and where shared national standards can improve their experience.

  • Review recruiting pipelines, conversion, producer retention, and market priorities.
  • Map the move from first conversation to producer integration and early productivity.
  • Establish a shared baseline for net growth, production added, and retention.

Outcome: An agreed diagnosis and a focused set of priorities.

TURN INSIGHT INTO A REPEATABLE MOTION

Give regional teams
a practical growth playbook.

Build with the people closest to the agents. Pilot a consistent national framework in selected markets, with flexibility for regional relationships and market dynamics.

  • Sharpen targeting, discovery, positioning, and follow-up.
  • Introduce coaching and a shared pipeline review cadence.
  • Align producer integration milestones and identify retention risks early.

Outcome: A working pilot, usable tools, and clear accountability.

LEARN BEFORE SCALING

Measure the quality
of growth, then refine.

Use the pilot to understand what improves conversion and activation. Pair early results with agent feedback and adjust before wider rollout.

  • Track net agent growth and net production added by market.
  • Review recruiting economics and newly joined producer productivity.
  • Identify retention signals and agree the next phase of rollout.

Outcome: An evidence-informed plan for scaling the growth function.

THE AGENT VALUE PROPOSITION

A promise that holds up
in the day-to-day.

Brand, support, and technology must translate into something a top producer can feel.

I’m interested in helping connect Elliman’s luxury heritage and its investment in technology to a clear, credible agent proposition. The question I would ask is practical: what helps an established producer serve clients better, run a stronger business, and want to stay?

With Elius and the Google Cloud technology initiative, I see an opportunity to work alongside the technology team to turn capabilities into agent value, adoption, and useful feedback. Trust is earned when the platform delivers on the pitch.

At UMass Amherst, I earned a B.S. in Resource Economics and competed as an NCAA Division I swimmer. The habits that sport demands—preparation, consistency, and accountability—continue to shape how I lead.
